correctness.rationale: For centered compound Poisson X of intensity lambda>0 and positive geometric jumps J with Pr(J=k)=(1-q)q^(k-1), the variance is V=lambda*(1+q)/(1-q)^2. The canonical second-order equilibrium factorization log Ee^(tX)=V*t²/2*E e^(tR) has R=M+U with M geometric on nonnegative integers, U independent density 2*(1-(1-q)u)/(1+q) for 0<u<1. Mean c=E R=(1+4q+q²)/(3(1-q²)). Direct stop-loss calculation gives cS(u)-F(u)=(1-q)² u(u-1)((1+q)u-1)/(3(1+q)²) on 0<=u<=1, so log(F(u)/c)+u/c has maximum at cell endpoint; F(0)=c and F(1)=q*c<c*exp(-1/c) using -log q>1/c. By geometric memorylessness F(m+u)=q^m F(u), proving R<=cx Exp(mean c) at every threshold. Thus Eexp(tR)<=(1-c t)^-1 for 0<=t<1/c, yielding the sub-gamma bound; comparing cubic Taylor coefficients with exact variance proxy enforces c>=kappa3/(3V)=given c. Formula is sharp for every q in (0,1), lambda>0. NBUE fails on part of (0,1) since F/S>c. Audited symbolic verifier and independently checked key polynomial and moment expressions; finite numerical grids alone do not establish convex order.
